docs.content:
Question: Do you go out every day?
Other ways to ask: Which days do you operate? / Are there trips every day of the year?
Answer: We operate every day of the year except December 25 and January 1. Trips are only suspended due to adverse weather conditions that affect safety.

Question: Do you offer private or closed group services?
Other ways to ask: How much does a private tour cost? / Can I book just for my group?
Answer: Private services and closed groups are available, with no fixed price (it depends on the group and the date). A member of our team prepares the quote and coordinates an available instructor for the date.

Question: What are your operating hours?
Other ways to ask: What time do the tours start and end? / Until what time are you open?
Answer: From Cartagena: departure at 8:00 a.m. from Muelle de la Bodeguita and return at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.). From the islands: hotel pick-up around 9:30 a.m. (7:30 a.m. on day 2 of some courses). Daytime activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m. (see the activity schedule). Night diving: in the evening (pick-up around 5:30 p.m., back around 7:30 p.m.). Online booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before; after that, you book on the website for the next available day.

Question: What's included in the tour?
Other ways to ask: What services are included in the tour? / What do I get when I book a tour with you?
Answer: All tours include: National Park entrance, dive insurance, boat transfer Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena (if departing from Cartagena), full equipment, and eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL. Lunch is included only on the first day for those departing from Cartagena. If you are already in the Rosario Islands, lunch is not included.

Question: What food is included in the tour?
Other ways to ask: Can I bring my own food? / Do you have options for vegetarians or people with allergies?
Answer: The tour includes water all day, coconut candy between dives, and lunch (rice with chicken or rice with vegetables). The menu is always the same, it does not change by day/supplier. Vegetarians, vegans, and celiacs receive rice with vegetables. Guests may bring their own food if needed (e.g. allergy or special diet). If the guest has a food allergy, they must inform us before the tour.

Question: Do you have availability tomorrow?
Other ways to ask: Are there spots for those dates? / Is there room on Saturday?
Answer: There is always availability (confirmed by the business). We only close on December 25 and January 1, and a trip can be suspended due to adverse weather. The date and number of people are chosen in the booking link. To book for the next day, you need to do it before 4:30 p.m. (see booking system cutoff).

Question: What food is included in the tour?
Other ways to ask: What kind of food is offered during the tour? / Is lunch included in the diving or snorkeling activity?
Answer: The tour includes water throughout the day, coconut candy between dives, and lunch (rice with chicken or rice with vegetables). Vegetarians, vegans, and those with celiac disease receive rice with vegetables. If you have any food allergy, you must inform us before the tour. Lunch is only included on the first day for those departing from Cartagena; for those already on the islands, lunch is not included.

Question: Do you offer private services or closed group trips?
Other ways to ask: Can I book a private or exclusive trip just for my group? / Is there an option for diving only with my group and no other people?
Answer: Yes, private services and closed group trips can be organized, with no fixed price (it depends on the group and the date). An advisor from the team will prepare a quote and coordinate an available instructor for the requested date.

docs.content:
Question: Is Isla Grande part of the Rosario Islands?
Other ways to ask: Does Isla Grande count as the Rosario Islands? / Is Isla Grande in the Rosario archipelago?
Answer: Yes. Isla Grande is one of the Rosario Islands, and it is where our dive base is (Hotel San Pedro de Majagua and Hotel Cocoliso).

Question: Is Barú the same as the Rosario Islands?
Other ways to ask: Are Barú and the Rosario Islands the same place? / Does Diving Planet operate in Barú or only in the Rosario Islands?
Answer: No. Barú is a continental peninsula connected to land, while the Rosario Islands are an archipelago of islands separated by sea, within the National Natural Park. They are different destinations. Diving Planet operates exclusively in the Rosario Islands, not in Barú.

Question: Do you have accommodation options in the Rosario Islands?
Other ways to ask: Where can I stay if I go diving with you in the Rosario Islands? / Is accommodation included in the diving plans or do I need to book it separately?
Answer: Our dive base is located at two hotels: Hotel San Pedro de Majagua and Hotel Cocoliso, both on Isla Grande (Rosario Islands). You can stay at either of these hotels for greater convenience, but it is not required. You may also choose other hotels in the area with maritime access or a nearby dock, such as Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras, and Pao Pao. Accommodation is not included in the diving plans and must be booked directly with the hotel.

Question: What reefs and corals are there in the Rosario Islands?
Other ways to ask: What types of corals and reefs can you see in the Rosario Islands? / What is the coral and reef life like in the Rosario Islands?
Answer: The Rosario Islands host some of Colombia's most important coral reefs. You can find coral gardens, coral walls, shallow reefs, rocky formations, and sandy channels between reefs. There are hard corals such as massive corals, brain corals, and pyramidal formations; also soft waving corals, barrel sponges, tube sponges, and large reef sponges. Colors can include yellow, purple, orange, blue, and green, creating very photogenic Caribbean reef landscapes.

Question: If I'm already on the islands, is there an extra charge for boat pick-up?
Other ways to ask: Is there any additional fee for boat pick-up if I'm staying on the islands? / Do I have to pay extra for boat transportation if my hotel is on the Rosario Islands?
Answer: No. If you are already on the Rosario Islands and your hotel has maritime access, boat pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge. The prices for plans for those already on the islands already account for the fact that there is no transport from Cartagena.

Question: Is pick-up from my hotel on the islands included?
Other ways to ask: Is boat transport from my hotel extra? / Can you pick me up if I'm already on the Rosario Islands?
Answer: If the guest is already on the Rosario Islands and their hotel has maritime access, boat pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge.

Question: Why choose the Rosario Islands for diving?
Other ways to ask: What are the advantages of diving in the Rosario Islands? / Why are the Rosario Islands recommended for diving?
Answer: The Rosario Islands combine Caribbean reefs, warm water, tropical marine life, and proximity to Cartagena. They are ideal for vacation diving, beginners, Open Water and Advanced courses, snorkeling, underwater photography, reef exploration, and relaxed recreational diving. The experience feels very Caribbean: boat ride from Cartagena, turquoise water, tropical islands, relaxed surface interval, and reefs full of fish. It is a convenient destination for combining vacation and diving without going far from the city.

Question: Which hotels on the Rosario Islands can you pick me up from?
Other ways to ask: From which hotels on the Rosario Islands can you pick me up for diving? / Can you pick me up at my hotel on the Rosario Islands?
Answer: Our dive base is at Hotel San Pedro de Majagua and Hotel Cocoliso, on Isla Grande. We also coordinate pick-up from other hotels in the area with maritime access, such as Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras, and Pao Pao. In some cases, the boat arrives directly at the hotel; in others, we indicate the nearest dock or meeting point, or a short walk to our dive center. If you are already on the islands, pick-up and return by boat are included at no extra charge if your hotel has maritime access. The pick-up point and time are coordinated by a team advisor.

docs.content:
Question: I have my certification card but I haven't dived in years. Do I need a refresher?
Other ways to ask: How long without diving before I need a refresher? / Do I need a refresher if I have my certification but haven't dived in years?
Answer: If you are a certified diver and have not dived for more than 2 years, a refresher is usually required to return to the water safely and confidently. Very experienced divers (over 500 dives or Dive Master level) may be evaluated by a team advisor to determine if the refresher is necessary. You can see the full itinerary for the refresher here: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/minicurso-principiantes/

Question: Do I need a refresh if I haven't dived in a long time?
Other ways to ask: Is a refresher mandatory if I haven't dived in years? / When do I need to do a refresher before diving again?
Answer: If you haven't dived in more than 2 years, a refresh is normally required to safely get back in the water. Very experienced divers (500+ logged dives, Dive Master) can be reviewed by a team advisor before booking. More info (full itinerary): https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/minicurso-principiantes/ If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly.

Question: It's been over two years since my last dive, do I need a refresher?
Other ways to ask: When is a refresher course required? / What if I haven't dived in a long time?
Answer: If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If they already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as their refresher and they can dive directly.

Service sheet: Refresher (review for certified divers who haven't dived in more than 2 years) — for guests already on the Rosario Islands (hotel pick-up if it has boat access)

The refresher is the SAME activity as the Dive Mini Course: same information, itinerary, requirements and price. It is booked as 'Dive Mini Course (already on the islands)'. Below is that mini course's sheet.

Review for certified divers who haven't dived in more than 2 years (no transport from Cartagena, no lunch).

Facts for Refresher: 134 USD / 475.000 COP online, 149 USD / 528.000 COP regular; 1 day; lunch NOT included; for already-certified divers; minimum age 10.

Included for Refresher:
- Hotel pick-up (if there is maritime/boat access)
- Dive insurance
- Diving equipment
- A PADI professional accompanying the activity

Itinerary for Refresher:
- Hotel pick-up between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (if your hotel has boat access)
- Transfer to our base and diving equipment setup
- Pool theory + practical session
- 1 open-water dive + surface interval at the base
- Return to your hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m.

Requirements for Refresher:
- Be ready at 9:30 a.m. at your hotel
- Be 10+ years old
- Complete the form sent in the confirmation email to process the insurance
- Complete the medical form (required for courses and mini-courses): https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol

Booking: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/dive-mini-course-already-on-island/20?language=es · More info: https://divingplanet.org/buceo-islas-del-rosario/

Service sheet: Refresher (review for certified divers who haven't dived in more than 2 years) — departing from Cartagena

The refresher is the SAME activity as the Dive Mini Course: same information, itinerary, requirements and price. It is booked as 'Dive Mini Course'. Below is that mini course's sheet.

Review for certified divers who haven't dived in more than 2 years.

Facts for Refresher: 183 USD / 655.000 COP online, 204 USD / 727.000 COP regular; 1 day; same-day round trip from Cartagena; boat Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena included; lunch included; for already-certified divers.

Included for Refresher:
- National Park entrance fee
- Mandatory dive insurance
- Boat transport Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena
- Pool training + 1 ocean dive with a PADI instructor
- Diving equipment
- Lunch
- Eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL

Not included for Refresher:
- Ground transportation to the dock
- Underwater photos or videos
- Voluntary tips
- Additional food beyond the included lunch
- Return on a different date

Itinerary for Refresher:
- Meeting point: Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. (5 min from the historic center)
- Speedboat transfer to the Rosario Islands (approx. 1 hour)
- Welcome at our island base
- Equipment setup + instructor support throughout
- Pool session: theory review and confined-water practice
- 1 reef dive + surface interval
- Lunch at the hotel facilities
- Return to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (estimated arrival 4:15 p.m.)

Requirements for Refresher:
- Complete the theory before starting the practical sessions
- After diving, wait at least 12 hours before flying
- Complete the medical form (required for courses and mini-courses): https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol

Before the activity for Refresher: After booking you'll receive an email with instructions to complete the theory. You must finish it before starting the practical sessions.

Booking: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=es · More info: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/minicurso-principiantes/

Question: Does the mini-course give certification?
Other ways to ask: Do I need anything from PADI for the mini-course? / What's included in the try-dive?
Answer: The mini-course is a one-day try-dive, an introduction to diving: it does not certify, does not count as part of any PADI course and requires nothing from PADI beforehand (no PADI account or PADI online course). After booking you receive the theory part by email, which must be completed before the activity; the day includes pool practice and 1 ocean dive with an instructor.

Question: Do I need to stay on the islands for the course?
Other ways to ask: Can I commute from Cartagena each day of the course? / Is accommodation included in the course?
Answer: Two-day courses (Open Water, Referral Course, Advanced) require accommodation on the islands. There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel.

Question: Which forms do I need to fill in before diving?
Other ways to ask: What documents do I need to complete before the diving activity? / Which forms are required before I can dive?
Answer: Before diving, you must complete two forms: the insurance form, which you receive in your booking confirmation email, and the liability waiver, which the team sends you to fill in (certified divers: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol). If you have not done it yet, the confirmation email reminds you.

Más información (itinerario completo): https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/minicurso-principiantes/ Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente.

Pregunta: Hace más de dos años que no buceo, ¿necesito un refresh?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cuándo es obligatorio hacer un refresco de buceo? / ¿Qué pasa si llevo mucho tiempo sin bucear?
Respuesta: Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh; los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) los revisa un asesor del equipo. Si ya hizo un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como su refresh y puede bucear directamente.

Pregunta: ¿Necesito hacer un refresh si llevo mucho tiempo sin bucear?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Es obligatorio hacer un refresh si llevo años sin bucear? / ¿Cuándo tengo que hacer un refrescamiento antes de bucear?
Respuesta: Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh para volver al agua con seguridad. Los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) pueden ser evaluados por un asesor del equipo antes de reservar. Más información (itinerario completo): https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/minicurso-principiantes/ Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente.

Pregunta: ¿Hay algún código de descuento?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Tienen un cupón de descuento? / ¿Qué código pongo para el descuento?
Respuesta: No existe ningún código de descuento. El 10 % de descuento se aplica directamente al reservar online en la web; el precio online ya lo lleva.

Pregunta: ¿Hay descuento por bucear dos días?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿El segundo día de buceo tiene algún beneficio? / ¿Qué descuento hay para el segundo día?
Respuesta: 10% de descuento para segundo día de buceo

Respuesta: Si eres buzo certificado y llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere realizar un refresh para volver al agua con seguridad y confianza. Los buzos muy experimentados (más de 500 inmersiones o nivel Dive Master) pueden ser evaluados por un asesor del equipo para determinar si el refresh es necesario. Puedes ver el minuto a minuto del refresh aquí: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/minicurso-principiantes/

Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cuáles son los servicios que no están cubiertos en el plan? / ¿Qué gastos adicionales debo considerar que no están incluidos?

Pregunta: ¿Qué no está incluido?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cuáles son los servicios que no están cubiertos en el plan? / ¿Qué gastos adicionales debo considerar que no están incluidos?
Respuesta: No está incluido: transporte terrestre al muelle, fotos y videos submarinos, propinas voluntarias, comida adicional al almuerzo, y el regreso a Cartagena en una fecha distinta a la del plan. Si el cliente desea regresar en una fecha diferente, lo coordina un asesor del equipo.

Pregunta: ¿Qué comida incluye el tour?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Qué tipo de comida ofrecen durante el tour? / ¿El almuerzo está incluido en la actividad de buceo o snorkel?
Respuesta: El tour incluye agua durante todo el día, dulces de coco entre inmersiones y almuerzo (arroz con pollo o arroz con vegetales). Los vegetarianos, veganos y celíacos reciben arroz con vegetales. Si tienes alguna alergia alimentaria, debes informarlo antes del tour. El almuerzo solo está incluido el primer día para quienes salen desde Cartagena; para quienes ya están en las islas, el almuerzo no está incluido.

Ficha del servicio: Servicio Privado — saliendo desde Cartagena

Datos de Servicio Privado: precio: lo cotiza un asesor; almuerzo NO incluido; sin certificación previa.

Más información: https://divingplanet.org/servicio-privado-buceo-cartagena/

Pregunta: ¿Qué incluye el tour?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Qué servicios están incluidos en el tour? / ¿Qué recibo al reservar un tour con ustedes?
Respuesta: Todos los tours incluyen: entrada al Parque Nacional, seguro de buceo, transporte en lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena (si la salida es desde Cartagena), equipo completo y aporte eco-social a DIVE TO HEAL. El almuerzo está incluido solo el primer día para quienes salen desde Cartagena. Si ya estás en las Islas del Rosario, el almuerzo no está incluido.

Pregunta: ¿Puede venir un acompañante que no bucea?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Mi pareja puede ir en la lancha aunque no se sumerja? / ¿Qué incluye el plan de acompañante? / ¿Cuánto paga alguien que solo acompaña?
Respuesta: Sí. El plan de acompañante es para quien no bucea ni hace snorkel y va en la lancha con el grupo. Saliendo desde Cartagena incluye la lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena, el almuerzo, el seguro y la entrada al Parque Nacional Natural. Si ya están en las islas, el acompañante va en la lancha con el grupo e incluye el seguro y la entrada al Parque Nacional Natural; el almuerzo no está incluido. El precio es el mismo saliendo desde Cartagena o ya en las islas (el del catálogo, con el 10 % de descuento online). Si lo prefiere, el acompañante puede quedarse en la isla, en nuestra base, mientras el grupo bucea. Ningún plan incluye alojamiento.

Pregunta: ¿Puedo regresar a Cartagena otro día?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cómo hago si quiero quedarme más días en la isla? / ¿El regreso en fecha diferente está incluido?
Respuesta: El regreso a Cartagena en una fecha distinta a la del plan no está incluido. Si el cliente quiere quedarse más días en las islas y volver con nosotros otro día, lo coordina un asesor del equipo (espacio en la lancha, etc.).

Pregunta: ¿Si ya estoy en las Islas del Rosario, me recogen en mi hotel?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Pueden recogerme en mi hotel si ya estoy en las islas? / ¿La recogida en el hotel está incluida si me hospedo en las Islas del Rosario?
Respuesta: Sí. Si ya estás en las Islas del Rosario y tu hotel tiene acceso marítimo, la recogida y el regreso en lancha están incluidos sin cargo adicional. En algunos casos la lancha llega directo al hotel; en otros, un asesor del equipo te indica el muelle o punto más cercano. Estos planes tienen precios diferentes porque no incluyen transporte desde Cartagena ni almuerzo (salvo el plan de acompañante, que cuesta lo mismo).

Ficha del servicio: Tour de Snorkeling — saliendo desde Cartagena

Plan de snorkeling para disfrutar del arrecife desde la superficie: 2 salidas guiadas con un guia local y almuerzo en las islas.

Datos de Tour de Snorkeling: 126 USD / 448.000 COP online, 140 USD / 497.000 COP normal; 1 día; ida y vuelta desde Cartagena el mismo día; lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena incluida; almuerzo incluido; sin certificación previa; edad mínima 6.

Incluye de Tour de Snorkeling:
- Tarifa de ingreso al Parque Nacional Natural
- Seguro de la actividad
- Transporte en lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena
- 2 salidas guiadas con guia local
- Equipo de snorkeling
- Almuerzo
- Aporte eco-social a DIVE TO HEAL

No incluye de Tour de Snorkeling:
- Transporte terrestre al muelle
- Fotos o videos
- Propinas voluntarias
- Comida adicional diferente al almuerzo incluido
- Regreso en una fecha distinta a la programada

Itinerario de Tour de Snorkeling:
- Punto de encuentro: Muelle de la Bodeguita a las 8:00 a.m. (a 5 min del centro historico)
- Traslado en lancha rapida (aprox. 1 hora) a las Islas del Rosario
- Bienvenida en nuestra base en las islas
- Entrega de equipo de snorkeling
- 2 salidas guiadas de snorkel + intervalo de superficie
- Almuerzo en las instalaciones del hotel
- Regreso a Cartagena a las 3:00 p.m. (llegada estimada 4:15 p.m.)

Requisitos de Tour de Snorkeling:
- Llegar puntual al punto de encuentro (8:00 a.m.)
- Edad mínima: 6 años

Reserva: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/superficio/3?language=es · Más información: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/tour-snorkeling/

docs.content:
Question: I'm vegetarian or have a food allergy. Can you accommodate me?
Other ways to ask: What food options do you have for vegetarians, vegans, or people with allergies? / Can I bring my own food if I have a special diet or allergies?
Answer: Yes. Vegetarians, vegans, and celiacs receive rice with vegetables for lunch. If you have a specific allergy (shellfish, gluten, nuts, etc.) or prefer to bring your own food, you're welcome to do so; just let us know before the tour so we can manage it. If you are already on the islands, lunch is not included in the plan.

Question: What food is included in the tour?
Other ways to ask: Can I bring my own food? / Do you have options for vegetarians or people with allergies?
Answer: The tour includes water all day, coconut candy between dives, and lunch (rice with chicken or rice with vegetables). The menu is always the same, it does not change by day/supplier. Vegetarians, vegans, and celiacs receive rice with vegetables. Guests may bring their own food if needed (e.g. allergy or special diet). If the guest has a food allergy, they must inform us before the tour.

Question: What food is included in the tour?
Other ways to ask: What kind of food is offered during the tour? / Is lunch included in the diving or snorkeling activity?
Answer: The tour includes water throughout the day, coconut candy between dives, and lunch (rice with chicken or rice with vegetables). Vegetarians, vegans, and those with celiac disease receive rice with vegetables. If you have any food allergy, you must inform us before the tour. Lunch is only included on the first day for those departing from Cartagena; for those already on the islands, lunch is not included.

Question: If I stay at Pao Pao, San Pedro de Majagua, or Cocoliso, can you pick me up?
Other ways to ask: Do you pick up at Pao Pao, San Pedro de Majagua, or Cocoliso hotel? / Can you arrange pick-up if I stay at Pao Pao, Majagua, or Cocoliso?
Answer: Yes. San Pedro de Majagua and Cocoliso are our island base, so pick-up there is confirmed. For Pao Pao, pick-up is also coordinated, but a team advisor needs to confirm the logistics with you first: depending on the hotel's maritime access, the boat may arrive directly or you may need to walk a short distance to the nearest dock. The exact pick-up point and time will be confirmed by a team advisor, who will also ask for your hotel name to coordinate it.

Question: Can I bring a suitcase on the boat?
Other ways to ask: Is there somewhere to store my luggage? / Is it just one bag per person?
Answer: Each person can bring one backpack or bag on the boat. If the guest needs to bring a suitcase, it has to be arranged with a member of our team. If they prefer not to take it, we can store the suitcase at our office in Cartagena.

Question: Do you have availability tomorrow?
Other ways to ask: Are there spots for those dates? / Is there room on Saturday?
Answer: There is always availability (confirmed by the business). We only close on December 25 and January 1, and a trip can be suspended due to adverse weather. The date and number of people are chosen in the booking link. To book for the next day, you need to do it before 4:30 p.m. (see booking system cutoff).

Question: Do I need to show my diver card to join?
Other ways to ask: Can I send you a picture of my certification? / What if I forget my diver card?
Answer: For recreational dive outings, you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.

Question: Do you offer private or closed group services?
Other ways to ask: How much does a private tour cost? / Can I book just for my group?
Answer: Private services and closed groups are available, with no fixed price (it depends on the group and the date). A member of our team prepares the quote and coordinates an available instructor for the date.

Question: Does the mini-course give certification?
Other ways to ask: Do I need anything from PADI for the mini-course? / What's included in the try-dive?
Answer: The mini-course is a one-day try-dive, an introduction to diving: it does not certify, does not count as part of any PADI course and requires nothing from PADI beforehand (no PADI account or PADI online course). After booking you receive the theory part by email, which must be completed before the activity; the day includes pool practice and 1 ocean dive with an instructor.

Question: What's the minimum age for diving?
Other ways to ask: Can kids join the activities? / From what age can you do the mini course?
Answer: It depends on the activity: snorkeling from 6 years old; Bubble Makers from 8 to 10 years old (pool mini-course and very shallow water practice, max 2 meters); the dive mini-course and PADI courses from 10 years old. Minors must be accompanied by a demonstrable parent or responsible relative.

Question: I want to get my diving certification, which course is it?
Other ways to ask: I want to become a certified diver / Which course do I need to get my diving license?
Answer: The full diver certification is the PADI Open Water (Basic) Course: it is what people usually mean by "getting certified" and it lets you dive with a certified buddy down to 18 meters. If you already did the theory and pool sessions at another center, you can finish it here with the Referral Course (Open Water). There is also the PADI Scuba Diver Course, a shorter, partial certification with which you always dive with a professional.

Question: What is the minimum age to participate?
Other ways to ask: From what age can children participate? / What is the minimum age for each diving or snorkeling activity?
Answer: The minimum age depends on the activity: for snorkeling, from 6 years old; for Bubble Makers, from 8 to 10 years old (mini-course in a pool and very shallow water, maximum 2 meters); for the dive mini-course and PADI courses, from 10 years old. Minors must be accompanied by a demonstrable parent or responsible relative.

Question: What is the maximum allowed diving depth?
Other ways to ask: How deep can I dive according to my certification? / What is the depth limit for each diving level?
Answer: The maximum depth depends on your level and always respects the limit of each certification: the mini-course or discover scuba allows up to 12 meters (typically between 5 and 12 meters); certified Open Water divers can go up to 18 meters; divers with Advanced certification (and advanced packages) up to 30 meters; the Bubble Makers program for children ages 8 to 10 reaches 2 meters. The actual depth of each dive depends on the selected dive site, always within your certification limit.

Question: What is the Bubble Makers program?
Other ways to ask: How does Bubble Makers work for kids? / From what age can children participate in Bubble Makers?
Answer: Bubble Makers is a PADI program designed for children ages 8 to 10 who want to safely try diving. The activity takes place in a pool or very shallow water (maximum 2 meters deep), always with a PADI instructor dedicated exclusively to them. It is the way for children of that age to get started in diving without needing prior certification. Children under 8 cannot do Bubble Makers or dive; they can only snorkel (from age 6). From age 10, they can participate in the regular dive mini-course or PADI courses.

Question: Is the PADI certification physical or digital?
Other ways to ask: Does PADI still issue physical certification cards? / How do I receive my PADI certification after the course?
Answer: The PADI certification is fully digital. PADI no longer issues physical cards; certification is delivered as an eCard (digital card) through the PADI app. The eCard is accepted for diving anywhere in the world.

Question: Do I need to stay on the islands for the course?
Other ways to ask: Can I commute from Cartagena each day of the course? / Is accommodation included in the course?
Answer: Two-day courses (Open Water, Referral Course, Advanced) require accommodation on the islands. There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel.

Question: Do 2-day courses require staying overnight on the islands?
Other ways to ask: Is it mandatory to stay overnight on the islands for 2-day courses? / Can I do the Open Water or Advanced course without staying on the islands?
Answer: Yes. Courses that last 2 days (such as Open Water and Advanced) require accommodation on the Rosario Islands. There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days, as the second day's itinerary starts directly on the islands. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel.

- Day 1: return to your hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m.

- Day 2: pool training + 2 open-water dives

El alojamiento no está incluido y debe reservarse directamente con el hotel.

Pregunta: ¿Cuáles son los horarios de operación?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿A qué hora salen y regresan los tours? / ¿Hasta qué hora están abiertos?
Respuesta: Desde Cartagena: salida a las 8:00 a.m. desde el Muelle de la Bodeguita y regreso a las 3:00 p.m. (llegada aprox. 4:15 p.m.). Desde las islas: recogida en el hotel hacia las 9:30 (a las 7:30 el día 2 de algunos cursos). Las actividades de día terminan hacia las 12:00-13:00 (ver el horario de las actividades). Buceo nocturno: por la tarde-noche (recogida hacia las 5:30 p.m. y regreso hacia las 7:30 p.m.). Sistema de reservas online cierra a las 4:30 p.m. del dia anterior; pasada esa hora se reserva por la web para el siguiente día disponible.

Pregunta: ¿Puedo regresar a Cartagena otro día?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cómo hago si quiero quedarme más días en la isla? / ¿El regreso en fecha diferente está incluido?
Respuesta: El regreso a Cartagena en una fecha distinta a la del plan no está incluido. Si el cliente quiere quedarse más días en las islas y volver con nosotros otro día, lo coordina un asesor del equipo (espacio en la lancha, etc.).

llamadas.respuesta:
¡Bacano que te animes con la certificación! El Curso Básico PADI (Open Water) dura 2 días. 🌊

El día 1 arrancas a las 8:00 a.m. desde el Muelle de la Bodeguita, haces piscina y tus primeras inmersiones, y duermes en las islas. El día 2 terminas las inmersiones finales y regresas a Cartagena a las 3:00 p.m. (llegada aprox. 4:15 p.m.).

Ojo con un detalle importante: como es de 2 días, hay que dormir al menos una noche en las Islas del Rosario. El alojamiento no está incluido, se reserva directo con el hotel.

docs.content:
Question: Are photos or videos included in the tour?
Other ways to ask: Can the instructor take pictures? / How much does it cost to get photos or videos?
Answer: Photos and videos are not offered proactively or included in the price. The instructor may take them voluntarily and delivers them by the next day at the latest. Any tip to the instructor for photos/videos is voluntary: each guest gives whatever they like, directly to them. Photos and videos are not taken during the mini-course (the first diving experience, for people who have never dived); on PADI courses (Open Water and others) and certified-diver trips the above applies: not included, the instructor may take them voluntarily.

Question: Do you take photos or videos during the activity?
Other ways to ask: Can I get photos or videos of my dive? / Are photos or videos included in the activities?
Answer: Our instructors may take photos and videos during the activity, but this is not a service offered automatically or included in the price. If the instructor does it, it is a voluntary gesture and is delivered by the next day at the latest. Any tip to the instructor for photos or videos is voluntary: each guest gives whatever they like, directly to them. Photos and videos are not taken during the mini-course or first-time experiences.

Question: Do I need to show my diver card to join?
Other ways to ask: Can I send you a picture of my certification? / What if I forget my diver card?
Answer: For recreational dive outings, you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.

Question: Is it good for underwater photography?
Other ways to ask: Are the Rosario Islands recommended for underwater photography? / Can you take good underwater photos during your dives?
Answer: Yes. The Rosario Islands are suitable for recreational photography thanks to colorful reefs, tropical fish, sponges, textures, soft corals, and coral walls. The destination works for wide-angle reef shots, fish photography, and simple macro photography. Photogenic subjects include parrotfish, soft corals, sponges, coral walls, schools of fish, and reef textures. Caribbean natural light helps create bright underwater conditions, especially on shallow reefs.

Question: Are snorkeling and diving groups together on the boat?
Other ways to ask: Do you split snorkelers and divers? / Where do snorkelers go if I'm with divers?
Answer: In groups combining diving and snorkeling, snorkeling takes place in a different area from the dive sites. If there are few people everyone goes on the same boat; otherwise the group is split by activity.

Question: Where can I see the options if I am already a certified diver?
Other ways to ask: What options are there for certified divers? / Where can I find diving plans for certified divers?
Answer: If you are already a certified diver, you can find all the details and book daily diving trips to the Rosario Islands at this link: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/2-buceos-1-dia/. Remember that to join recreational diving trips, you must present your diver certification card, either by sending a photo in advance or showing it on the day of the activity.

Question: Can mixed groups (certified divers, beginners, and snorkelers) join the same tour?
Other ways to ask: Can a group with certified divers, beginners, and snorkelers do activities together on the same day? / Is it possible to mix certified divers, mini-course participants, and snorkelers in one tour?
Answer: Yes, it is possible to combine different activities in one tour. Groups can include certified divers, people who want to do the mini-course, and those who only want to snorkel. While certified divers do their first dive or snorkelers do their first activity, mini-course participants do their theory and pool training. On the second dive, if they wish, they can join the mini-course participants for the open water dive. In groups that combine diving and snorkeling, snorkeling is done in a different area from diving. If there are few people, they go together in the same boat; otherwise, they are divided by activity. More info: https://divingplanet.org/en/fun-dives-snorkeling-cartagena/

Question: What recommendations should I follow for a diving day in the Rosario Islands?
Other ways to ask: What should I bring or keep in mind for diving in the Rosario Islands? / Any practical tips for a diving day in the islands?
Answer: It is recommended to bring reef-safe sunscreen, stay hydrated throughout the day, use sunglasses and sun protection, and consider seasickness tablets if you are sensitive to boats. An underwater camera can be useful if you want photos of reefs and fish. For the water, light tropical exposure protection is usually enough because the temperature is around 28°C, although everyone tolerates cold differently. It is important not to touch coral or wildlife, maintain good buoyancy, and always follow the guide or instructor's directions.

docs.content:
Question: What time does the activity finish?
Other ways to ask: What time does the course end on the first day? / Will I have time to enjoy the hotel in the afternoon? / What time do we get back to Cartagena?
Answer: All daytime activities (dive trips, mini-course, snorkeling, courses and each day of the packages) end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., followed by lunch. Guests departing from Cartagena have lunch included on the islands and the boat returns to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.); guests staying on the islands return to their hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m. for lunch (lunch not included). On overnight courses and packages, day 1's daytime activities also end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., and then you go to your hotel on the islands. Night diving (on plans that include it) is separate, in the evening (see each plan's schedule).

Question: What are your operating hours?
Other ways to ask: What time do the tours start and end? / Until what time are you open?
Answer: From Cartagena: departure at 8:00 a.m. from Muelle de la Bodeguita and return at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.). From the islands: hotel pick-up around 9:30 a.m. (7:30 a.m. on day 2 of some courses). Daytime activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m. (see the activity schedule). Night diving: in the evening (pick-up around 5:30 p.m., back around 7:30 p.m.). Online booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before; after that, you book on the website for the next available day.

Question: What are your operating hours?
Other ways to ask: What time do your diving activities start and end? / What are the opening and closing times for activities from Cartagena and from the islands?

docs.content:
Question: Where do I fill out the waiver form?
Other ways to ask: Will you send me the form to sign? / Is the waiver required to dive?
Answer: Besides the insurance form, each diver fills in a liability waiver. Our team sends it to you to complete, and the confirmation email reminds you if you have not done it yet.

Question: Which forms do I need to fill in before diving?
Other ways to ask: What documents do I need to complete before the diving activity? / Which forms are required before I can dive?
Answer: Before diving, you must complete two forms: the insurance form, which you receive in your booking confirmation email, and the liability waiver, which the team sends you to fill in (certified divers: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol). If you have not done it yet, the confirmation email reminds you.

Question: Do I need to fill out a medical form?
Other ways to ask: Are there any medical restrictions for diving? / What are the medical requirements for courses?
Answer: The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. If you are a certified diver, there are no additional medical restrictions; your liability waiver is the certified-diver one: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.

Service sheet: Open Water Referral Course - already on the islands — for guests already on the Rosario Islands (hotel pick-up if it has boat access)

If you already completed the theory and pool sessions at your local PADI center, you can finish your Open Water certification in 2 days while diving in the Rosario Islands.

Facts for Open Water Referral Course - already on the islands: 432 USD / 1.565.000 COP online, 480 USD / 1.740.000 COP regular; 2 days; lunch NOT included; no prior certification; minimum age 10.

Included for Open Water Referral Course - already on the islands:
- Hotel pick-up (if there is maritime/boat access)
- Entry to the Rosario Islands Natural Park
- Mandatory dive insurance
- 4 certification dives with a PADI instructor
- Full diving equipment
- Surface intervals with access to hotel facilities
- PADI certification
- Eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL

Not included for Open Water Referral Course - already on the islands:
- Ground transportation to the dock
- Boat transfer Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena
- Hotel/accommodation on the Rosario Islands
- Underwater photos or videos
- Voluntary tips
- Meals (lunch not included)
- Any other service not specified

Itinerary for Open Water Referral Course - already on the islands:
- Phase 1: theory + pool sessions completed at your home PADI dive center
- Day 1: hotel pick-up between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (if your hotel has boat access) + referral paperwork check
- Day 1: transfer to our base + theory review + equipment check
- Day 1: 2 certification dives
- Day 1: return to your hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m.; overnight on the islands (hotel not included)
- Day 2: hotel pick-up at 7:30 a.m. (if your hotel has boat access)
- Day 2: 2 final dives
- Day 2: return to your hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m. + certification processing

Requirements for Open Water Referral Course - already on the islands:
- Have completed the theory and pool sessions at your home PADI dive center
- Bring your referral paperwork signed by a PADI instructor
- After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying

Before the activity for Open Water Referral Course - already on the islands: You must arrive with the theory and pool sessions completed at your home dive center and bring your referral paperwork signed by a PADI instructor.

More info: https://divingplanet.org/curso-padi-cartagena/referido/

Service sheet: Refresher (review for certified divers who haven't dived in more than 2 years) — departing from Cartagena

The refresher is the SAME activity as the Dive Mini Course: same information, itinerary, requirements and price. It is booked as 'Dive Mini Course'. Below is that mini course's sheet.

Review for certified divers who haven't dived in more than 2 years.

Facts for Refresher: 183 USD / 655.000 COP online, 204 USD / 727.000 COP regular; 1 day; same-day round trip from Cartagena; boat Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena included; lunch included; for already-certified divers.

Included for Refresher:
- National Park entrance fee
- Mandatory dive insurance
- Boat transport Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena
- Pool training + 1 ocean dive with a PADI instructor
- Diving equipment
- Lunch
- Eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL

Not included for Refresher:
- Ground transportation to the dock
- Underwater photos or videos
- Voluntary tips
- Additional food beyond the included lunch
- Return on a different date

Itinerary for Refresher:
- Meeting point: Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. (5 min from the historic center)
- Speedboat transfer to the Rosario Islands (approx. 1 hour)
- Welcome at our island base
- Equipment setup + instructor support throughout
- Pool session: theory review and confined-water practice
- 1 reef dive + surface interval
- Lunch at the hotel facilities
- Return to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (estimated arrival 4:15 p.m.)

Requirements for Refresher:
- Complete the theory before starting the practical sessions
- After diving, wait at least 12 hours before flying
- Complete the medical form (required for courses and mini-courses): https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol

Before the activity for Refresher: After booking you'll receive an email with instructions to complete the theory. You must finish it before starting the practical sessions.

Booking: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=es · More info: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/minicurso-principiantes/

Other ways to ask: What activities can I do with Diving Planet? / What services does Diving Planet offer in Cartagena? / How much experience do you have? / Why should I dive with you?
Answer: Diving Planet is a PADI 5-Star dive center with 30 years of experience in Cartagena. We operate in the Rosario Islands Coral Reefs National Natural Park and offer dive trips for certified divers, a mini-course for beginners, PADI courses, and snorkeling tours. By diving with Diving Planet, you also support Dive To Heal, an initiative for coral restoration and adaptive diving.

Service sheet: Open Water Referral Course — departing from Cartagena

If you already completed the theory and pool sessions at your local PADI center, you can finish your Open Water certification in 2 days while diving in the Rosario Islands.

Facts for Open Water Referral Course: 474 USD / 1.680.000 COP online, 526 USD / 1.867.000 COP regular; 2 days; you must stay overnight on the islands (lodging not included), not a same-day round trip; boat Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena included; lunch on day 1 only; no prior certification.

Included for Open Water Referral Course:
- Entry to the Rosario Islands Natural Park
- Mandatory dive insurance
- Roundtrip boat transfer Cartagena-Islands
- 4 certification dives with a PADI instructor
- Full diving equipment
- Surface intervals with access to hotel facilities
- Lunch on day 1
- PADI certification
- Eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL

Not included for Open Water Referral Course:
- Ground transportation to the dock
- Hotel/accommodation on the Rosario Islands
- Underwater photos or videos
- Voluntary tips
- Additional food beyond the included lunch
- Any other service not specified

Itinerary for Open Water Referral Course:
- Phase 1: theory + pool sessions completed at your home PADI dive center
- Day 1: meeting point at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. + referral paperwork check
- Day 1: speedboat transfer to the Rosario Islands (approx. 1 hour)
- Day 1: welcome at our base + theory review + equipment check
- Day 1: 2 certification dives + lunch (included)
- Day 1: activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.; then transfer to the hotel where you'll stay overnight on the islands (hotel not included)
- Day 2: 2 final dives + lunch (not included)
- Day 2: return to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (estimated arrival 4:15 p.m.) + certification processing

Requirements for Open Water Referral Course:
- Have completed the theory and pool sessions at your home PADI dive center
- Bring your referral paperwork signed by a PADI instructor
- After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying

Before the activity for Open Water Referral Course: You must arrive with the theory and pool sessions completed at your home dive center and bring your referral paperwork signed by a PADI instructor.

More info: https://divingplanet.org/curso-padi-cartagena/referido/

Question: I lost my diving certification card. Can I still dive?
Other ways to ask: I don't have my diver card, can I join the dive trip? / What should I do if I can't find my diving certification?
Answer: If you do not have your certified diver card, an advisor from the team can help you look up your certification in your certifying agency's database. You will need to provide the agency (PADI, NAUI, CMAS, etc.), your full name, and your email address. Certification is required to participate in recreational diving trips.

Answer: Diving Planet is a PADI 5-Star dive center with 30 years of experience in Cartagena. We operate in the Rosario Islands Coral Reefs National Natural Park and offer dive trips for certified divers, a mini-course for beginners, PADI courses, and snorkeling tours. By diving with Diving Planet, you also support Dive To Heal, an initiative for coral restoration and adaptive diving.

Question: Where are you located?
Other ways to ask: What is the address of Diving Planet in Cartagena? / Where is the Diving Planet office located?
Answer: Our main office is at Plaza de San Diego, Calle 39 #8-24, second floor (above Juan Valdez), Walled City, Cartagena de Indias, Colombia.

Question: What is the meeting point?
Other ways to ask: Where should I go for the activity? / What time and where is the meeting point for the diving trip?
Answer: The meeting point is Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, at 8:00 a.m. You do not need to queue; just ask for DIVING PLANET at entrance 3. Location: https://www.google.com/maps/place/Muelle+de+la+Bodeguita/@10.4199447,-75.5537609,828m/data=!3m2!1e3!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x8ef62f753729822d:0x1bbcdd8224d0eaaf!8m2!3d10.4199447!4d-75.551186!16s%2Fg%2F113gzkckf?entry=ttu

Question: When is high season?
Other ways to ask: What dates are considered high season for diving? / When is there more demand or high season at Diving Planet?
Answer: High season is from December 20 to January 15, during Holy Week, and in July and August. However, the center operates year-round with excellent conditions.

Question: Where do you dive?
Other ways to ask: In which location do you do the dives? / Where are your dive sites located?
Answer: We dive in the Rosario Islands, inside the Corales del Rosario y San Bernardo National Natural Park, about 45-60 minutes by boat from Cartagena. It is one of the most popular diving destinations in the Colombian Caribbean: a protected tropical archipelago of approximately 27 islands, with coral reefs, warm water year-round, Caribbean marine life, and relaxed profiles for recreational diving, courses, snorkeling, and underwater photography.

Question: What is the maximum allowed diving depth?
Other ways to ask: How deep can I dive according to my certification? / What is the depth limit for each diving level?
Answer: The maximum depth depends on your level and always respects the limit of each certification: the mini-course or discover scuba allows up to 12 meters (typically between 5 and 12 meters); certified Open Water divers can go up to 18 meters; divers with Advanced certification (and advanced packages) up to 30 meters; the Bubble Makers program for children ages 8 to 10 reaches 2 meters. The actual depth of each dive depends on the selected dive site, always within your certification limit.

Question: On the 2-dive trip, do we dive at the same site? How long is each dive?
Other ways to ask: Are the two dives at different spots? / How long do you stay underwater on each dive? / Does it cost more to dive at two different sites?
Answer: The 2 dives are done at two different dive sites. If the day's conditions require changing the site, the instructor decides on the day. Each dive lasts 40 to 50 minutes. The price doesn't change for diving at different sites: it is included in the plan price.

Question: I want to get my diving certification, which course is it?
Other ways to ask: I want to become a certified diver / Which course do I need to get my diving license?
Answer: The full diver certification is the PADI Open Water (Basic) Course: it is what people usually mean by "getting certified" and it lets you dive with a certified buddy down to 18 meters. If you already did the theory and pool sessions at another center, you can finish it here with the Referral Course (Open Water). There is also the PADI Scuba Diver Course, a shorter, partial certification with which you always dive with a professional.

docs.content:
Pregunta: ¿En qué moneda se paga?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Puedo pagar en dólares o solo en pesos colombianos? / ¿Hay un precio diferente para colombianos o extranjeros?
Respuesta: Los colombianos (vivan donde vivan) y los residentes en Colombia pagan en pesos colombianos (COP). El resto de clientes internacionales paga en dólares estadounidenses (USD). El precio es el mismo en ambas monedas; solo cambia la moneda de pago. No existe un descuento especial por ser colombiano.

Pregunta: ¿El precio es diferente para colombianos?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Puedo pagar en pesos si soy colombiano? / ¿Hay descuento por ser residente en Colombia?
Respuesta: Pagan en pesos colombianos (COP) los colombianos (vivan donde vivan) y los residentes en Colombia (también quien tiene cédula de extranjería, que es un documento de residente). El resto de clientes internacionales paga en dólares (USD). El precio es el mismo: solo cambia la moneda (no hay descuento por ser colombiano).

Pregunta: ¿Puedo pagar en pesos colombianos si soy colombiano?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Hay algún descuento especial para colombianos? / ¿Los precios son diferentes para extranjeros y colombianos?
Respuesta: Los clientes colombianos y residentes en Colombia pagan en pesos colombianos (COP). Los clientes internacionales pagan en dólares (USD). No hay un descuento especial por ser colombiano; el precio es el mismo, solo cambia la moneda.

Pregunta: ¿Puedo pagar en euros? ¿Cuánto cuesta en euros?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Aceptan pagos en euros o solo en dólares? / ¿Puedo pagar la actividad en euros o tengo que pagar en otra moneda?
Respuesta: No manejamos precios en euros. Los clientes internacionales, incluidos los europeos, pagan en dólares americanos (USD). Tu banco o tarjeta hará la conversión de USD a euros automáticamente al momento del pago. Si eres colombiano o residente en Colombia, el pago se realiza en pesos colombianos (COP). El precio es el mismo en ambas monedas, solo cambia la moneda según tu nacionalidad o residencia.

Pregunta: ¿Los colombianos pagan diferente?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Hay un precio especial para colombianos? / ¿Pagan menos los colombianos o residentes en Colombia?
Respuesta: Los colombianos (vivan donde vivan) y los residentes en Colombia pagan en pesos colombianos (COP). El resto de clientes internacionales paga en dólares (USD). En un grupo mixto (colombianos o residentes y extranjeros), toda la reserva se paga en USD. El precio es el mismo para todos: solo cambia la moneda. No existe descuento especial por ser colombiano. Puedes reservar directamente desde nuestra página web con el 10% de descuento online.

Pregunta: ¿Qué pasa si en mi grupo hay colombianos y extranjeros?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cómo se paga si somos un grupo mixto? / ¿El precio cambia si hay residentes y turistas juntos?
Respuesta: Si en el grupo hay colombianos o residentes y también extranjeros, toda la reserva del grupo se paga en dólares (USD), al mismo precio equivalente. No hay un precio distinto por ser colombiano.

Pregunta: ¿Qué medios de pago aceptan?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cómo puedo pagar mi reserva? / ¿Qué formas de pago están disponibles para reservar?
Respuesta: Los colombianos y los residentes en Colombia (también con cédula de extranjería) pueden pagar el 100% en línea, o un anticipo del 50% en línea con métodos de pago colombianos (incluyendo Llave, el sistema de pagos instantáneos de Bancolombia/ACH), y el otro 50% de forma presencial con tarjeta o efectivo. El resto de clientes extranjeros paga el 100% con tarjeta en la página web (con tarjeta extranjera se usa el pasaporte como documento de identificación). No se aceptan PayPal, criptomonedas ni pagos a plazos/cuotas.

Pregunta: ¿Hay que pagar todo de una vez o se puede dar un anticipo?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Puedo reservar pagando solo una parte y el resto después? / ¿Es obligatorio pagar el total al reservar o puedo dar solo un adelanto?
Respuesta: El método de pago depende de tu nacionalidad. Los colombianos y los residentes en Colombia (también con cédula de extranjería) pueden pagar el 100% en línea, o un anticipo del 50% en línea y el otro 50% de forma presencial (tarjeta o efectivo). El resto de clientes extranjeros debe pagar el 100% al reservar, utilizando una tarjeta extranjera en la página web y el pasaporte como documento de identificación. El anticipo del 50% solo aplica a colombianos y residentes en Colombia.

Pregunta: ¿En qué moneda se paga?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Puedo pagar en dólares o solo en pesos colombianos? / ¿Hay un precio diferente para colombianos o extranjeros?
Respuesta: Los colombianos (vivan donde vivan) y los residentes en Colombia pagan en pesos colombianos (COP). El resto de clientes internacionales paga en dólares estadounidenses (USD). El precio es el mismo en ambas monedas; solo cambia la moneda de pago. No existe un descuento especial por ser colombiano.

Pregunta: ¿El precio es diferente para colombianos?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Puedo pagar en pesos si soy colombiano? / ¿Hay descuento por ser residente en Colombia?
Respuesta: Pagan en pesos colombianos (COP) los colombianos (vivan donde vivan) y los residentes en Colombia (también quien tiene cédula de extranjería, que es un documento de residente). El resto de clientes internacionales paga en dólares (USD). El precio es el mismo: solo cambia la moneda (no hay descuento por ser colombiano).

Pregunta: ¿Puedo pagar en pesos colombianos si soy colombiano?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Hay algún descuento especial para colombianos? / ¿Los precios son diferentes para extranjeros y colombianos?
Respuesta: Los clientes colombianos y residentes en Colombia pagan en pesos colombianos (COP). Los clientes internacionales pagan en dólares (USD). No hay un descuento especial por ser colombiano; el precio es el mismo, solo cambia la moneda.

Pregunta: ¿Puedo pagar en euros? ¿Cuánto cuesta en euros?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Aceptan pagos en euros o solo en dólares? / ¿Puedo pagar la actividad en euros o tengo que pagar en otra moneda?
Respuesta: No manejamos precios en euros. Los clientes internacionales, incluidos los europeos, pagan en dólares americanos (USD). Tu banco o tarjeta hará la conversión de USD a euros automáticamente al momento del pago. Si eres colombiano o residente en Colombia, el pago se realiza en pesos colombianos (COP). El precio es el mismo en ambas monedas, solo cambia la moneda según tu nacionalidad o residencia.

Pregunta: ¿Los colombianos pagan diferente?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Hay un precio especial para colombianos? / ¿Pagan menos los colombianos o residentes en Colombia?
Respuesta: Los colombianos (vivan donde vivan) y los residentes en Colombia pagan en pesos colombianos (COP). El resto de clientes internacionales paga en dólares (USD). En un grupo mixto (colombianos o residentes y extranjeros), toda la reserva se paga en USD. El precio es el mismo para todos: solo cambia la moneda. No existe descuento especial por ser colombiano. Puedes reservar directamente desde nuestra página web con el 10% de descuento online.

Pregunta: ¿Qué pasa si en mi grupo hay colombianos y extranjeros?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cómo se paga si somos un grupo mixto? / ¿El precio cambia si hay residentes y turistas juntos?
Respuesta: Si en el grupo hay colombianos o residentes y también extranjeros, toda la reserva del grupo se paga en dólares (USD), al mismo precio equivalente. No hay un precio distinto por ser colombiano.

Pregunta: ¿Qué medios de pago aceptan?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Cómo puedo pagar mi reserva? / ¿Qué formas de pago están disponibles para reservar?
Respuesta: Los colombianos y los residentes en Colombia (también con cédula de extranjería) pueden pagar el 100% en línea, o un anticipo del 50% en línea con métodos de pago colombianos (incluyendo Llave, el sistema de pagos instantáneos de Bancolombia/ACH), y el otro 50% de forma presencial con tarjeta o efectivo. El resto de clientes extranjeros paga el 100% con tarjeta en la página web (con tarjeta extranjera se usa el pasaporte como documento de identificación). No se aceptan PayPal, criptomonedas ni pagos a plazos/cuotas.

Pregunta: ¿Hay que pagar todo de una vez o se puede dar un anticipo?
Otras formas de preguntarlo: ¿Puedo reservar pagando solo una parte y el resto después? / ¿Es obligatorio pagar el total al reservar o puedo dar solo un adelanto?
Respuesta: El método de pago depende de tu nacionalidad. Los colombianos y los residentes en Colombia (también con cédula de extranjería) pueden pagar el 100% en línea, o un anticipo del 50% en línea y el otro 50% de forma presencial (tarjeta o efectivo). El resto de clientes extranjeros debe pagar el 100% al reservar, utilizando una tarjeta extranjera en la página web y el pasaporte como documento de identificación. El anticipo del 50% solo aplica a colombianos y residentes en Colombia.

busquedas.query: Instead of the 5 dive package, do you have an option of just 2 day dives from Cartagena, so I only do one day?

docs.content:
Question: Can I do just 1 dive from Cartagena?
Other ways to ask: Is it possible to book just one dive departing from Cartagena? / Do you offer the option of a single dive from Cartagena?
Answer: From Cartagena, the minimum is 2 dives (a full-day trip), as the boat logistics and trip timing do not allow for a single dive. The option for just one dive is only available if you are already on the Rosario Islands, or in exceptional cases depending on availability, which is coordinated by a team advisor.

Question: What are my options if I don't want to do the night dive included in the package?
Other ways to ask: Can I swap the night dive for only daytime dives in my package? / What should I do if I don't want the night dive included in my package?
Answer: If you do not wish to do the night dive included in the packages, you can choose the 4 Daytime Dives Package, which consists of 4 daytime dives over 2 days, with no night dive. This package is available both for departures from Cartagena and for those already on the islands. In the 5, 7, and 9 dive packages, the night dive is included; if you prefer not to do it, the alternative is to switch to the 4 Daytime Dives Package.

Service sheet: 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive) — departing from Cartagena

Package for certified divers from Cartagena: 2 daytime dives + 1 night dive in one day of activities. You must stay on the island that night and hotel is not included.

Facts for 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive): 287 USD / 1.017.000 COP online, 319 USD / 1.130.000 COP regular; 1 day; includes a night dive; you must stay overnight on the islands (lodging not included), not a same-day round trip; boat Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena included; lunch included; certification required.

Included for 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive):
- National Park entrance fee
- Mandatory dive insurance
- Speedboat transport Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena
- 3 guided dives with a certified PADI professional
- Diving equipment
- Lunch on day 1
- Eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL

Not included for 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive):
- Ground transportation to the dock
- Hotel/accommodation on the Rosario Islands
- Lunches not explicitly included
- Underwater photos or videos
- Voluntary tips
- Additional food beyond the included lunch
- Any other service not specified

Itinerary for 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive):
- Day 1: meeting point at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. + speedboat transfer (approx. 1 hour)
- Day 1: arrival at our island base + equipment setup
- Day 1: 2 dives + surface interval + lunch (included)
- Day 1: 1 night dive
- Day 1: after the activity, you must stay at your selected island hotel (hotel not included)

Requirements for 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive):
- Be a certified diver and bring your certification card
- For this tour you must stay 1 night on the Rosario Islands because it includes a night dive (hotel not included)
- After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying

More info: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/

Service sheet: 5 Dives - 2 days — departing from Cartagena

Package for certified divers with 1 night on the Rosario Islands: 4 daytime dives + 1 night dive (bioluminescence). Hotel is not included.

Facts for 5 Dives - 2 days: 392 USD / 1.429.000 COP online, 436 USD / 1.587.000 COP regular; 2 days; includes a night dive; you must stay overnight on the islands (lodging not included), not a same-day round trip; boat Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena included; lunch on day 1 only; certification required.

Included for 5 Dives - 2 days:
- National Park entrance fee
- Mandatory dive insurance
- Speedboat transport Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena
- 5 guided dives with a certified PADI professional
- Diving equipment
- Lunch on day 1
- Eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL

Not included for 5 Dives - 2 days:
- Ground transportation to the dock
- Hotel/accommodation on the Rosario Islands
- Lunches not explicitly included
- Underwater photos or videos
- Voluntary tips
- Additional food beyond the included lunch
- Any other service not specified

Itinerary for 5 Dives - 2 days:
- Day 1: meeting point at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. + speedboat transfer (approx. 1 hour)
- Day 1: arrival at our island base + equipment setup
- Day 1: 2 dives + surface interval + lunch (included)
- Day 1: 1 night dive
- Day 1: transfer to your selected island hotel (hotel not included)
- Day 2: transfers between your hotel and our island base
- Day 2: 2 open-water dives
- Day 2: lunch (not included)
- Day 2: return to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (estimated arrival 4:15 p.m.)

Requirements for 5 Dives - 2 days:
- Be a certified diver and bring your certification card
- With this plan you must stay 1 night on the Rosario Islands (hotel not included)
- After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying

Booking: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/2-days-5-dives/9?language=es · More info: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/5-buceos-2-dias/

Question: Can I do an extra dive in addition to my package?
Other ways to ask: Is it possible to add an extra dive to my diving package? / Can I do an additional dive if I already have a package?
Answer: There is an option to add an extra dive, but in practice there is almost never enough time within the boat schedule to do so. It is not available at all from Cartagena for this same reason. Actual availability must be confirmed by a team advisor before assuming it is possible.

Service sheet: 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives) — departing from Cartagena

Package for certified divers with 1 night on the Rosario Islands: 4 daytime dives over 2 days. Hotel is not included.

Facts for 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 316 USD / 1.154.000 COP online, 351 USD / 1.282.000 COP regular; 2 days; you must stay overnight on the islands (lodging not included), not a same-day round trip; boat Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena included; lunch on day 1 only; certification required.

Included for 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives):
- National Park entrance fee
- Mandatory dive insurance
- Speedboat transport Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena
- 4 guided dives with a certified PADI professional
- Diving equipment
- Lunch on day 1
- Eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL

Not included for 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives):
- Ground transportation to the dock
- Hotel/accommodation on the Rosario Islands
- Lunches not explicitly included
- Underwater photos or videos
- Voluntary tips
- Additional food beyond the included lunch
- Any other service not specified

Itinerary for 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives):
- Day 1: meeting point at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. + speedboat transfer (approx. 1 hour)
- Day 1: arrival at our island base + equipment setup
- Day 1: 2 dives + surface interval + lunch (included)
- Day 1: transfer to your selected island hotel (hotel not included)
- Day 2: transfers between your hotel and our island base
- Day 2: 2 open-water dives
- Day 2: lunch (not included)
- Day 2: return to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (estimated arrival 4:15 p.m.)

Requirements for 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives):
- Be a certified diver and bring your certification card
- With this plan you must stay 1 night on the Rosario Islands (hotel not included)
- After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying

More info: https://divingplanet.org/tours-buceo-snorkel-cartagena/

Service sheet: 5-dive package (2 days) - already on the islands — for guests already on the Rosario Islands (hotel pick-up if it has boat access)

Package for certified divers already on the Rosario Islands (no transport from Cartagena, no lunch): 2 daytime dives + 1 night dive on day 1, and 2 daytime dives on day 2.

Facts for 5-dive package (2 days) - already on the islands: 319 USD / 1.000.000 COP online, 354 USD / 1.110.000 COP regular; 2 days; includes a night dive; lunch NOT included; certification required; minimum age 10.

Included for 5-dive package (2 days) - already on the islands:
- Hotel pick-up (if there is maritime/boat access)
- Dive insurance
- Diving equipment
- A PADI professional accompanying the activity

Itinerary for 5-dive package (2 days) - already on the islands:
- Day 1: hotel pick-up between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (if your hotel has boat access)
- Day 1: transfer to our dive center for fitting and equipment setup
- Day 1: 2 open-water dives + surface interval at the base
- Day 1: return to your hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m.
- Day 1: pick-up at 5:30 p.m. (if your hotel has boat access)
- Day 1: 1 night dive
- Day 1: return to your hotel around 7:30 p.m.
- Day 2: hotel pick-up between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (if your hotel has boat access)
- Day 2: transfer to our dive center for fitting and equipment setup
- Day 2: 2 open-water dives + surface interval at the base
- Day 2: return to your hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m.

Requirements for 5-dive package (2 days) - already on the islands:
- Be ready at 9:30 a.m. at your hotel
- Bring your diving certification card
- If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team
- Complete the form sent in the confirmation email to process the insurance
- Wait at least 18 hours before flying after diving

Booking: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/package-of-5-dives-already-on-island/21?language=es · More info: https://divingplanet.org/buceo-islas-del-rosario/

Service sheet: 7 Dives - 3 days — departing from Cartagena

Package for certified divers with 2 nights on the Rosario Islands: 6 daytime dives + 1 night dive (bioluminescence). Hotel is not included.

Facts for 7 Dives - 3 days: 503 USD / 1.813.000 COP online, 558 USD / 2.015.000 COP regular; 3 days; includes a night dive; you must stay overnight on the islands (lodging not included), not a same-day round trip; boat Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena included; lunch on day 1 only; certification required.

Included for 7 Dives - 3 days:
- National Park entrance fee
- Mandatory dive insurance
- Speedboat transport Cartagena-Islands-Cartagena
- 7 guided dives with a certified PADI professional

Question: Where is the meeting point?
Other ways to ask: What time and where do we meet for the trip? / Where is Muelle de la Bodeguita located?
Answer: Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, at 8:00 AM.

Question: What time is the departure?
Other ways to ask: What time should I arrive for departure? / What are the meeting and return times?
Answer: The meeting point is at 8:00 a.m. at Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center. The estimated return to Cartagena is at 4:15 p.m.

Question: What is the meeting point?
Other ways to ask: Where should I go for the activity? / What time and where is the meeting point for the diving trip?
Answer: The meeting point is Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, at 8:00 a.m. You do not need to queue; just ask for DIVING PLANET at entrance 3. Location: https://www.google.com/maps/place/Muelle+de+la+Bodeguita/@10.4199447,-75.5537609,828m/data=!3m2!1e3!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x8ef62f753729822d:0x1bbcdd8224d0eaaf!8m2!3d10.4199447!4d-75.551186!16s%2Fg%2F113gzkckf?entry=ttu

Question: What happens if I arrive late and the boat has already left?
Other ways to ask: Do I lose my reservation if I don't arrive at the dock on time? / What happens if I don't get there before the boat leaves?
Answer: If you arrive late and the boat has already left, there is no refund. The meeting point is at 8:00 a.m. at Muelle de la Bodeguita and departure is on time. It is recommended to arrive at least 10-15 minutes early.

Question: If I stay at Pao Pao, San Pedro de Majagua, or Cocoliso, can you pick me up?
Other ways to ask: Do you pick up at Pao Pao, San Pedro de Majagua, or Cocoliso hotel? / Can you arrange pick-up if I stay at Pao Pao, Majagua, or Cocoliso?
Answer: Yes. San Pedro de Majagua and Cocoliso are our island base, so pick-up there is confirmed. For Pao Pao, pick-up is also coordinated, but a team advisor needs to confirm the logistics with you first: depending on the hotel's maritime access, the boat may arrive directly or you may need to walk a short distance to the nearest dock. The exact pick-up point and time will be confirmed by a team advisor, who will also ask for your hotel name to coordinate it.

Question: Do you have availability tomorrow?
Other ways to ask: Are there spots for those dates? / Is there room on Saturday?
Answer: There is always availability (confirmed by the business). We only close on December 25 and January 1, and a trip can be suspended due to adverse weather. The date and number of people are chosen in the booking link. To book for the next day, you need to do it before 4:30 p.m. (see booking system cutoff).

Question: What are your operating hours?
Other ways to ask: What time do the tours start and end? / Until what time are you open?
Answer: From Cartagena: departure at 8:00 a.m. from Muelle de la Bodeguita and return at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.). From the islands: hotel pick-up around 9:30 a.m. (7:30 a.m. on day 2 of some courses). Daytime activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m. (see the activity schedule). Night diving: in the evening (pick-up around 5:30 p.m., back around 7:30 p.m.). Online booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before; after that, you book on the website for the next available day.

Question: Do you offer private or closed group services?
Other ways to ask: How much does a private tour cost? / Can I book just for my group?
Answer: Private services and closed groups are available, with no fixed price (it depends on the group and the date). A member of our team prepares the quote and coordinates an available instructor for the date.
